beats.hindi_tts: Murphy stresses: a moving average is strictly trend-following; it never anticipates or predicts.
beats.en_subtitle: Murphy stresses: a moving average is strictly trend-following; it never anticipates or predicts.

leftColumn.title: The Smoothing Purpose
leftColumn.subtitle: Filtering Out Day-to-Day Noise
bullets: Blunts volatile spikes to reveal underlying trend
Acts as dynamic dynamic support and resistance
Works brilliantly in defined trending phases

rightColumn.title: The Time Lag Reality
rightColumn.subtitle: Constructed Entirely on Past Data
bullets: Signals always occur AFTER turn has begun
Longer period equals larger lag behind price
Fails miserably in sideways, non-trending chop

beats.en_narration: Murphy stresses: a moving average is strictly trend-following; it never anticipates or predicts.

beats.hindi_tts: Shorter length increases sensitivity but multiplies whipsaws; longer length adds safety but delays entries.
beats.en_subtitle: Shorter length increases sensitivity but multiplies whipsaws; longer length adds safety but delays entries.

leftColumn.title: Short Average (e.g. 10-Day)
leftColumn.subtitle: High Sensitivity / High Whipsaw
bullets: Hugs price tightly for rapid response
Triggers repeated false signals during ranges
Best for aggressive short-term momentum

rightColumn.title: Long Average (e.g. 50/200-Day)
rightColumn.subtitle: High Smoothness / Pronounced Lag
bullets: Filters out false market head-fakes cleanly
Surrenders significant chunk of early move
Gold standard for institutional trend bias

beats.en_narration: Shorter length increases sensitivity but multiplies whipsaws; longer length adds safety but delays entries.

subtitlePhrases.text: Shorter length increases sensitivity but multiplies whipsaws;

beats.hindi_tts: A Simple Moving Average weights every day equally, whereas an EMA assigns greater weight to recent prices.
beats.en_subtitle: A Simple Moving Average weights every day equally, whereas an EMA assigns greater weight to recent prices.

leftColumn.title: Simple Moving Average (SMA)
leftColumn.subtitle: Equal Weighting Model
bullets: Sum of N days closing prices divided by N
Treats 50-day-old price identically to yesterday
Suffers 'drop-off effect' when old outlier falls off

rightColumn.title: Exponential Moving Average (EMA)
rightColumn.subtitle: Weighted Toward Recent Data
bullets: Multiplier = 2 / (N + 1)
Reacts swiftly to new price shocks
Never completely drops historical data

beats.en_narration: A Simple Moving Average weights every day equally, whereas an EMA assigns greater weight to recent prices.

subtitlePhrases.text: A Simple Moving Average weights every day equally,

beats.hindi_tts: The SMA drop-off effect distorts the average without fresh news, leading traders to favor the EMA.
beats.en_subtitle: The SMA drop-off effect distorts the average without fresh news, leading traders to favor the EMA.

leftColumn.title: SMA Drop-off Flaw
leftColumn.subtitle: Artificial shifts caused by past exits
bullets: Dropping an extreme outlier abruptly bends the curve
Curve bends even if current price is flat
Murphy: Major theoretical criticism of SMA

rightColumn.title: EMA Smooth Transition
rightColumn.subtitle: Continuous exponential decay
bullets: Smooth weighting avoids sudden drop-off spikes
Faster turns at key market reversal levels
Foundation for MACD and modern momentum tools

beats.hindi_tts: To neutralize false breakouts and whipsaws, Murphy recommends applying price and time filters.
beats.en_subtitle: To neutralize false breakouts and whipsaws, Murphy recommends applying price and time filters.

cards.title: 1. Price Filter (Percentage Rule)
cards.subtitle: Require price to clear the MA line by a minimum threshold (e.g., 1% or 3%) before acting

cards.title: 2. Time Filter (Multi-Day Rule)
cards.subtitle: Demand 2 or 3 consecutive closes beyond the moving average to validate the crossover

cards.title: 3. Combined Dual Filter
cards.subtitle: Close must satisfy both 1% margin AND hold for 2 consecutive sessions

ui_state.heading: Today's thread
steps: Moving averages are lagging, trend-following smoothing devices
Shorter averages yield rapid signals but multiply whipsaws
Longer averages provide reliable trend bias at the cost of lag
SMA weights all days equally, suffering from the drop-off effect
EMA weights recent price action exponentially, turning faster
Double crossovers smooth out raw price noise between two averages
50 and 200-day SMAs serve as global institutional benchmarks
Price (1-3%) and Time (2-day) filters eliminate sideways false signals
ui_state.bottomTakeaway: A moving average never predicts the future; it quantifies the present trend and enforces systematic discipline.
